g.text: Wallet creation with the key exported at creation
wallet: none → creating → ready_unsaved → ready_saved | ready_skipped (C14, C15, C16, C20; H-001, H-005, H-024, H-263)
The client request id dedupes a double tap (C14, H-007).
One keychain call at a time per home (C20).
rows: creating · keychain_write [kc_up and item == 'empty'] → creating;
[the account already holds an item (planted or older, H-024)]
row: creating · keychain_write [kc_up and item != 'empty'] → dropped
[the keychain cannot answer (prompt, locked, no Secret Service)]
At restart: creating · restart → ready_unsaved or dropped,
by what the keychain holds under A (Reconcile).
Save your key at creation (requirement 5; the creating client, C16)
The ready commit above also minted a creation capability bound to the create
request id: consumed once, within 10 min, on that request's own connection, before
the address is shown. No OS re-authentication is needed, so this works on a Linux
desktop, in a loopback browser of `banda serve` and on the host TTY of
`banda wallet create`. No daemon route reveals a key to a token alone.
A later reveal (OD-2): not on the daemon's HTTP API (C16, INV-S8)
The key is shown in a BrowserWindow that loads a bundled local file (sandboxed,
context isolation, no network, strict CSP, content protection) over preload IPC,
never the daemon's origin: a script in the web UI or a request with the owner's
Created from a paired phone: allowed, the wallet stays Not backed up and the phone says
"see the key on your computer" (H-276). The agent never gets a key tool (H-265).
